methods.label: Calculate and repeatedly halve
methods.explanation:
Repeatedly dividing by \(2\) will show how many factors of \(2\) the number contains. First evaluate the fourth powers by squaring twice:

\[13^4-11^4=28{,}561-14{,}641=13{,}920.\]

Starting with \(13{,}920\), successive divisions by \(2\) give

\[6{,}960,\quad3{,}480,\quad1{,}740,\quad870,\quad435.\]

These are five exact divisions. The final quotient, \(435\), is odd, so there is no sixth factor of \(2\). Thus

\[13^4-11^4=2^5\cdot435,\]

and the largest power of \(2\) that divides it is \(\boxed{32}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses whole-number powers, subtraction, and repeated halving; parity of the final quotient proves maximality.
